> 復。亨。出入無疾，朋來無咎。反復其道，七日來復。

Hexagram 24 is the turn after the erosion, and its character is a fifth instance of the same mishandling.

## 復 is 從彳，复聲

說文: 復，往來也。從彳，复聲.

Phonetic: 彳 (walking) as the semantic side, 复 as the sound.

Original sense: going and coming — leaving and returning.

The transmitted draft says "in bronze script, 彳 plus 畐, walking back to where one started," which treats 复 as a semantic component. That is a fifth time the same thing happens: 訟 從言公聲, 謙 從言兼聲, 觀 從見雚聲, 賁 從貝卉聲, now 復 從彳复聲 — plus one case in the other direction, 剝's dropped 亦聲.

Six instances, one conclusion. If the structure of the character is not settled, interpretation steps in and replaces the character's sense.

## 七日來復

Seven days to return.

Not a week as a unit of time, but a rhythm: the yang lines were stripped to the last one in 剝, and here the first one comes back at the bottom. The cycle has a period, and the period is stated.

Which makes 復's good news structural rather than emotional. The return is not a reversal of fortune; it is the shape of the cycle arriving on schedule.

## 不遠復

初九 不遠復，無祗悔，元吉.

祗 is great (大). 無祗悔: not arriving at a great regret.

To return while still near — before the distance has become a story.

And this is the best line in the hexagram: 元吉, at the very bottom. The earliest correction is the strongest.

## 休復 / 頻復 / 敦復

休: good, and at rest (美善、安止). 休復 is returning without strain — unhurried, not forced.

頻: repeatedly. 頻復 is being pulled back and forth: losing the way, coming back, losing it again. 厲 — dangerous — and 無咎.

敦: thick, honest. 敦復 is a return rooted in a substantial character, so that it does not need to be willed each time.

Three grades of the same act, distinguished by what is underneath it: ease, oscillation, weight.

## 中行獨復

六四 中行獨復.

Walking in the middle of the way, while everyone else is still in the yin, one person alone notices and turns back.

There is no judgement attached — no 吉, no 凶. The line simply records the position. Which is accurate: at that moment there is nothing to reward, and nothing to blame. The act is solitary by construction.

## 迷復

Top line: 迷復，凶，有災眚.

迷 — lost, and not returning. Going on down the wrong road.

災眚: 災 is disaster from outside; 眚 is the misfortune one's own blindness generates. The line has both, and the second is the operative one.

And the line continues: 用行師，終有大敗；以其國，君凶。至於十年不克征.

Ten years without being able to march. Which is the book's longest stated recovery period, and it is attached to the failure of not turning back — not to a defeat in the field.

## 至日閉關

The 象: on the solstice, close the passes.

冬至, when one yang first stirs. Close the borders, rest, do not disturb the fragile yang.

This is the hexagram's practical instruction, and it is the opposite of what a returning cycle usually prompts. The moment of return is not the moment to push. The new thing is one line at the bottom of five yin lines; it needs to be left alone.

## 天地之心

The 彖: 天地無心，以生生為心.

Heaven and earth have no mind of their own; their mind is making things live.

And the return of yang after the last one was stripped is that mind becoming visible.

So 復 is not "recovery." It is the demonstration that the cycle has a bias — that it produces, and produces again.

## The test

Take a correction you have been meaning to make. Ask how far away it still is: 不遠復 or the long road. The hexagram's grades are all about distance, and the top line's ten years is what distance becomes when it stops being measured.
